title: Graphs of Inverse Trigonometric Functions & Their Derivatives (AA HL)

sections.heading: Section 1: Domains and Ranges of Inverse Trig Functions

questions.q: What are the domain and range of the principal arcsine function $y = \arcsin x$?
questions.answer: To make sine invertible, its domain is restricted to $[-\pi/2, \pi/2]$ with range $[-1, 1]$. Thus $\arcsin x$ has domain $[-1, 1]$ and range $[-\pi/2, \pi/2]$.

questions.q: What are the domain and range of $y = \arccos x$?
questions.answer: The cosine function is restricted to $[0, \pi]$ where it is strictly decreasing. Therefore $\arccos x$ maps $[-1, 1]$ onto $[0, \pi]$.

questions.q: What are the horizontal asymptotes of the graph of $y = \arctan x$?

sections.heading: Section 2: Derivatives of Inverse Trigonometric Functions

questions.q: What is the derivative of $f(x) = \arcsin(3x)$ for $|x| < \frac{1}{3}$?
What is the relationship between the derivatives of $\arcsin x$ and $\arccos x$?
choices: They are reciprocals of each other
questions.answer: Because $\arcsin x + \arccos x = \frac{\pi}{2}$ for all $x \in [-1, 1]$, differentiating both sides yields $\frac{d}{dx}[\arccos x] = -\frac{d}{dx}[\arcsin x]$.

sections.heading: Section 3: Tangent Lines and Extreme Values

questions.q: Find the slope of the tangent line to $y = \arcsin x$ at $x = 0$.
What happens to the slope of $y = \arcsin x$ as $x \to 1^-$?
questions.answer: As $x \to 1^-$, $\sqrt{1 - x^2} \to 0^+$, so $y'(x) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}} \to +\infty$, resulting in a vertical tangent at the boundary.

questions.q: Find the equation of the tangent line to $y = \arctan x$ at $x = 1$.
questions.answer: Point is $(1, \arctan 1) = (1, \pi/4)$. Derivative is $y'(1) = \frac{1}{1 + 1^2} = \frac{1}{2}$. Tangent line: $y - \frac{\pi}{4} = \frac{1}{2}(x - 1)$.

sections.heading: Section 4: Integration Producing Inverse Trig Functions

questions.answer: Factor out 4: $\sqrt{4(1 - 9x^2/4)} = 2\sqrt{1 - (3x/2)^2}$. Let $u = 3x/2, du = 3/2 dx \Rightarrow dx = 2/3 du$. Integral: $\frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{2}{3} \int \frac{du}{\sqrt{1 - u^2}} = \frac{1}{3}\arcsin(u) + C = \frac{1}{3}\arcsin(3x/2) + C$.
